target.title: fix(agents): keep background exec exit notifications UTF-16 safe at the snippet cut
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who enable background exec exit notifications (`notifyOnExit`) can receive a broken/replacement character (�) in their chat channel. When a completed background command's tail output overflows the notification snippet limit and an emoji lands exactly at the truncation cut, the delivered `Exec completed/failed (…) :: <output>` message ends with a dangling half of a UTF-16 surrogate pair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notification snippet compactor truncated with a raw `String.slice(0, limit - 1)`, which can cut a surrogate pair in half. This swaps it for the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (the same helper already used for tool-description summaries in #98644, model-picker labels, etc.), so truncation never splits an astral code point. There is no behavior change for ASCII/BMP output.

## User Impact

Background exec completion notifications delivered to chat channels no longer show a broken character when the last visible characters include an emoji at the truncation boundary. Ordinary output and the existing truncation ellipsis are unchanged.

## Evidence

`compactNotifyOutput` in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` is only reached from `maybeNotifyOnExit`, which enqueues the system event that is delivered to the session's channel, so the defect is entirely in the string the runtime hands to delivery (before transport).

Added a focused regression in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts` that drives the real notify path (`runExecProcess` → backgrounded exit → `enqueueSystemEvent`) with tail output where an emoji's high surrogate lands at index 178, so a raw `slice(0, 179)` keeps the dangling half.

- before (pre-fix source on `upstream/main`): the enqueued message ends with a lone surrogate — `Exec failed (…, signal SIGKILL) :: aaaa…aaaa�…` — and the test (which asserts against a lone-surrogate regex) FAILS.
- after (this change): the same real path yields no lone surrogate; the snippet stays truncated with `…` and keeps the readable head.

Commands run in a worktree off `upstream/main`:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts -t "UTF-16 boundary"` → pass
- negative control: `git checkout HEAD -- src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` then re-run the test → fails on the lone-surrogate assertion, then restored the fix
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `oxfmt --check`, and `oxlint` on the changed files → all pass

What was not tested: no live channel round-trip (e.g. Telegram/Discord delivery) was exercised. The defect is before transport, in the snippet string the runtime enqueues, so the focused real-path test captures it; the full suite runs in CI.

AI-assisted: implemented and validated with AI assistance; the commands and outputs above were run for real.
